document.title: Letter of GOP Permrep to SYG on Afghanistan (USUN N 004283)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Unclassified] Reproduces an October 25, 1995 letter from Pakistan's UN representative to the UN Secretary General. It reaffirms Pakistan's claimed neutral stance in intra-Afghan rivalries and its support for UN and OIC peace efforts, illustrating Pakistan's public position.

persons.name: Ahmad Kamal
persons.role: Permanent Representative of Pakistan (GOP) to the United Nations; author of 25 Oct 1995 letter to the UN Secretary-General

mentions.quote: TEXT OF OCTOBER 25 LETTER TO UNSYG FROM : GOP PERMREP AHMAD KAMAL

persons.name: Ismail Khan
persons.role: Former governor of Herat, defeated by the Taliban at Herat in 1995

mentions.quote: GENERAL ISMAIL KHAN, THE FORMER GOVERNOR OF HERAT, IN HIS INTERVIEW WITH THE BRITISH BROADCASTING CORPORATION HAS CATEGORICALLY DENIED PAKISTAN'S INVOLVEMENT

persons.name: Burhanuddin Rabbani
persons.role: President of the Kabul government (called the 'junta' in the letter)

mentions.quote: PROFESSOR RABBANI HAS TIME AND AGAIN RENEGED ON HIS COMMITMENT TO HAND OVER POWER TO A TRANSITIONAL AUTHORITY
CONTINUED INTRANSIGENCE OF PROFESSOR RABBANI AND AHMED SHAD MASOUD TO COOPERATED WITH AMBASSADOR MESTIRI

persons.name: Mahmoud Mestiri
persons.role: UN Special Envoy/Ambassador mediating transfer of power in Afghanistan

mentions.quote: TO COOPERATED WITH AMBASSADOR MESTIRI IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE UNITED NATIONS PLAN FOR THE PEACEFUL TRANSFER OF POWER

events.description: Afghan Vice-Minister for Foreign Affairs wrote to the UNSG alleging Pakistani support for the Taliban (S/1995/866).
Pakistan Permrep Ahmad Kamal sent letter to the UN Secretary-General denying Pakistani support for the Taliban.
Taliban captured Herat and western Afghanistan; Ismail Khan defeated; 25-30 casualties reported.
Taliban advanced in Charasyab owing to defections of Kabul regime commanders.
Afghan Vice-Minister for Foreign Affairs sends a letter to the UN Secretary-General alleging Pakistani support for the Taliban (S/1995/866).
Ahmad Kamal sends a letter to the UN Secretary-General rejecting the allegations and urging cooperation with Mestiri and the OIC.
The Taliban capture Herat and western Afghanistan with about 25-30 casualties; Ismail Khan is defeated.
The Taliban advance at Charasyab owing to defections of Kabul regime commanders.

sources_cited: S/1995/866 letter of Afghan Vice-Minister for Foreign Affairs, 12 Oct 1995
key_claims: Pakistan's UN envoy denies supporting the Taliban and claims neutrality in intra-Afghan rivalries.
Pakistan argues the Taliban took western Afghanistan and Herat with little resistance (25-30 casualties), reflecting disenchantment with Kabul.
Pakistan cites Ismail Khan's BBC interview as denying Pakistani involvement in his Herat defeat.
Pakistan blames Rabbani and Massoud for obstructing the UN transfer-of-power plan.
The Taliban advance in Charasyab is attributed to defections of Kabul regime commanders.
Pakistan says the Kabul government controls only 5 of 32 provinces and hosts 1.5 million Afghan refugees.
